name: Wedding
blurbs: {customer} needs something posh for a wedding, and the bride is forty minutes late already.
{customer} has booked the church, the cake and the band, but the wedding car firm has folded.
{customer} wants a grand arrival that will make Aunt Jean put down the tea.
success: {car} swept up to the church as the bells rang, and {customer} wept into a very good hankie.
The photographs came out beautifully; even the photographer admitted {car} was the best-dressed thing present.
{customer} arrived in style, and two separate guests asked for the number of whoever owns it.
mishap: {customer} reversed {car} into the manor hedge while rehearsing the speech, and the topiary has opinions.
The best man was sick in the boot of {car}, and it was the confetti-covered corner, too.
{car} lost a hubcap down the lane, and {customer} led a wedding party search for it.
disaster: A startled flock of churchyard pigeons used {car} as a confetti cannon, and {customer} has cancelled the reception.
{customer}'s Uncle Nigel towed a trailer with {car}, and the bull inside has now seen the whole village.

name: Magazine photo shoot
blurbs: {customer} is styling a magazine shoot and needs a classic that photographs well by eleven o'clock.
{customer} needs a motor for a magazine spread, and the art director hates everything sensible.
{customer} is shooting a fashion editorial at a stately home and insists only a classic will do.
success: The photographer circled {car} for an hour and declared it the muse of the season.
{customer} got the cover shot, mostly thanks to {car} catching the light just so.
The stylist only retouched the lipstick twice, and {car} looks briefly immortal in print.
mishap: {customer} parked {car} in the tractor calendar shoot's spot, and there is now a scheduling war.
A wind machine toppled onto {car}, leaving it lightly draped in expensive designer silk.
{customer}'s assistant waxed {car} with the wrong stuff and it gleams like a boiled sweet.
disaster: The sprinkler system chose the exact moment {car} was perfectly positioned, and {customer} has quit the whole editorial.
Escaped farm animals from the next field licked {car} into a matte finish while {customer} watched, helpless.

name: Classic car show (concours)
blurbs: {customer} is showing at the concours and needs something with pedigree, correct badges and no excuses.
{customer} has a concours lawn spot, and the club chairman is famously unforgiving about patina.
{customer} needs a proper classic for the show, as the judges have brought binoculars this year.
success: {car} took the class trophy, and the club chairman wrote its number down approvingly.
{customer} accepted a rosette the size of a dinner plate on {car}'s behalf.
Three separate judges used the word "original", and {car} has never been so admired.
mishap: {car} stalled while coasting past the judges' stand, and {customer} performed a quiet bow to cover it.
{customer} was caught polishing {car} with the wrong cloth, and a retired colonel has written a letter.
A wasp nest formed in {car}'s door pocket overnight, and {customer} discovered this mid-judging.
disaster: The display ramp collapsed beneath {car} during judging, dropping it into the ornamental fish pond in front of {customer}.
Bees from a neighbouring hive moved into {car}'s exhaust, and {customer} is now a formal matter for the beekeepers.

name: TV costume drama
blurbs: {customer} is producing a television costume drama and needs a carriage that actually goes.
{customer} needs a period-appropriate motor for a Sunday night drama, and the director keeps saying "authenticity".
{customer} is filming a costume drama in the village, and the lead actress refuses anything modern.
success: {car} delivered {customer}'s duchess to the manor gate without a single anachronism in frame.
The director called {car} the finest supporting actor on set, and {customer} got the shot.
{customer}'s drama wrapped early, because {car} required no retakes whatsoever.
mishap: {car} backfired during the emotional deathbed scene, and {customer} has decided it is now canon.
{customer} parked {car} in shot of a satellite dish, and continuity has filed a formal complaint.
The leading man's cape snagged on {car}'s door handle, and the take is ruined for everyone.
disaster: The flood scene used real river water, and {car} is now technically a narrowboat; {customer} has gone very quiet.
A fog machine with attitude exploded beside {car}, and {customer}'s leading lady has left for a rival drama.

name: Rock band music video
blurbs: {customer} is managing a rock band that needs a classic car for their new music video. They promise to be gentle. They will not be gentle.
It's {customer} here. Our band wants to lip-sync on the bonnet of something classy for the video. Smoke machines are involved.
{customer} needs a beautiful old car for a music video shoot. The lead singer insists on standing on the roof. Please say yes.
success: The band loved {car} so much they wrote a song about it. {customer} pays in full and promises to send a copy of the DVD.
The shoot wrapped early because {car} upstaged the lead singer. {customer} hands over the fee and a torn backstage lanyard.
{car} looked magnificent in the video and the single crept to number forty. {customer} reports the bonnet has barely any footprints.
mishap: The smoke machine set off the fire alarms and the shoot was cut short. {customer} still got the chorus, somehow.
The drummer used {car} as a drum riser. The roof survived. The drummer didn't get paid, and {customer} asks for a discount.
{customer}'s band mistook {car} for a props van and filled the boot with foam fingers. It took three hours to vacuum out.
disaster: The pyrotechnics went off early and scorched the paintwork. {car} now smells of burnt guitar strings, and {customer} has vanished behind a wall of dry ice.
The band's tour bus rolled backwards over {car} during the big finale, and {customer} says the insurance covers 'artistic differences'.

name: Stag do driving day
blurbs: {customer} has organised a stag do and wants a proper old car for a day of country lanes. What could possibly go wrong?
It's {customer}: eight chaps, one classic car, and a spirit level for the drinking games. We leave at dawn.
{customer} needs something sturdy for a brother's stag do. The best man has promised to behave. Nobody believes him.
success: All eight of them came back with {car} intact and only mild sunburn. {customer} calls it the best day of the groom's life.
{car} managed the whole route with just one hubcap missing, and {customer} swears the groom wept with joy at the wheel.
The country lanes were kind and {car} handled them beautifully. {customer} has already asked about hiring something for the next wedding.
mishap: The best man reversed {car} into a hedge while parking 'for a laugh'. The hedge came off worse, and so did his dignity.
{customer} dropped the keys in a river, then found them in the groom's pocket. {car} waited patiently.
Someone fed the groom a pub chilli and the boot of {car} became an emergency. {customer} pays a little less and apologises a lot.
disaster: The stag tried a handbrake turn on a farm track and ploughed into a flock of sheep. {car} is wearing wool, and {customer} faces a farmer with strong opinions.
Half the stag party ended up in a duck pond with {car}, and {customer} says the vicar who fished them out has asked for danger money.

name: School prom arrival
blurbs: {customer}'s daughter wants to arrive at the school prom like royalty, and the other parents have already hired limousines. No pressure.
It's {customer}. The prom theme is 'old Hollywood' and my son wants a proper classic car to match. He has been practising his wave.
{customer} needs something elegant for a school prom. The teenagers will be taking four hundred photographs, minimum.
success: {car} swept up to the school gates like a film premiere, and {customer} says the teenager was voted best arrival at prom, earning {car} a round of applause.
The pupils applauded as {car} glided past, and {customer} says the daughter has finally forgiven the family for the estate car.
Every photograph at the prom ended up featuring {car}. {customer} has had one framed and pays the fee with a thank-you card.
mishap: {car}'s door stuck at the school gates and the teenager had to climb out in a ball gown. {customer} filmed it, and now it is on the noticeboard.
A dinner lady mistook {car} for the head's own car and tried to give it a parking ticket. {customer} talked her down, eventually.
The corsage caught in {car}'s window and there was a small shrieking incident. {customer} pays slightly less and apologises twice.
disaster: The school photographer reversed into {car} during the grand arrival, and {customer} spent the evening mediating between him and a head teacher with a clipboard.
A swarm of bees took a liking to {car}'s radiator grille just as the prom queen arrived, and {customer} had to explain the screaming to the sixth form.

name: Film villain getaway
blurbs: {customer} is producing a spy film and needs a classic car for the villain's getaway. There will be a controlled skid. Probably.
It's {customer} from the film studio. Our villain needs something elegant and menacing for the final chase across the moors.
{customer} wants a classic car for one getaway scene: a bank, a chase, and a stuntman who insists he has done this before.
success: The getaway scene was nailed in two takes, and {customer} says {car} is the most menacing thing on screen since the last villain.
The director fell in love with {car} and rewrote the ending so the villain escapes. {customer} pays in full and promises cinema tickets.
The stunt went perfectly and {car} drifted round the market square like a professional. {customer} applauds. The crew applauds. A seagull applauds.
mishap: The villain's coat caught in {car}'s door and the take was lost to laughter. {customer} says the outtakes alone are worth the fee.
A controlled skid turned out to be rather less controlled than advertised, and {car} took out two traffic cones. {customer} pays for the cones.
{customer}'s leading man insisted on doing his own driving and flattened a market barrow. The take was, everyone agrees, unforgettable.
disaster: The stunt went spectacularly wrong and {car} ended up in the canal alongside a rubber shark. {customer} is calling the scene "the villain's watery end".
A generator burst on set and covered {car} in green paint meant for the monster suit. {customer} has stopped answering the production phone.

name: Retirement surprise
blurbs: {customer} here. We are surprising a colleague who retires on Friday, and we want to collect them from the office in something splendid.
It's {customer}. The retirement do needs a proper classic car to deliver the guest of honour, and they must not find out. They won't. Probably.
{customer} needs a lovely old car for a retirement surprise. There will be a banner, a cake, and forty people hiding behind a van.
success: The retirement collectee arrived in {car} to a cheer that startled the postman, and {customer} reports there was not a dry eye in the car park.
{car} glided up to the gates with the banner flapping proudly, and {customer} says the retiree has told the story eleven times since.
The surprise went off without a hitch, and {customer} insists {car} now counts as a family member. The fee arrives with a slice of cake taped to the envelope.
mishap: The retiree spotted everyone hiding behind the van two streets early, and {customer} had to improvise a very unconvincing car boot sale.
{car} arrived wearing most of a paper banner, and {customer} spends the afternoon unpeeling sticky tape from the windscreen.
A colleague reversed into a hedge while filming the surprise on their phone, and {customer} asks quietly if the hedge is covered.
disaster: The surprise banner jammed in {car}'s windscreen wipers, the retiree honked the horn in panic, and a nearby flock of pigeons made everything worse while {customer} watched.
The retirement cake was travelling in the boot of {car} when the driver took a corner, and {customer} now faces a village fete committee armed with icing and grievances.

name: Estate agent brochure
blurbs: {customer} is selling a manor house and wants a classic car parked on the gravel for the brochure photo. Three hours, one driveway, endless angles.
It's {customer} from the estate agency. My seller insists the brochure has a beautiful old car outside, or they will not sign. Their words, not mine.
{customer} needs something dignified for an estate agent photo shoot. The property has a fountain, a peacock and a seller with strong opinions.
success: The brochure photograph came out so well that the house sold in a week, and {customer} swears it was {car} that sealed the deal.
{car} posed on the gravel like it had been to drama school, and {customer} reports the buyers kept asking if the car came with the house.
{customer} pays in full and sends a copy of the brochure, in which {car} has somehow upstaged a twelve-bedroom manor.
mishap: The peacock took a liking to {car}'s bonnet and refused to move for two hours, and {customer} has the photographs to prove it.
The seller insisted on leaning on {car} for every photograph, and {customer} spends the morning politely repositioning an elbow.
A garden sprinkler caught {car} mid-shoot and the "stately home" look became a "damp Tuesday" look. {customer} pays a little less and laughs a lot.
disaster: The gravel driveway hid a pothole of legend, {car} sank to the axles in front of the buyers, and {customer} had to describe it as a "period feature".
The prize bull escaped during the photo shoot and used {car} as a scratching post, and {customer} now must explain to both the farmer and the sellers.

name: Mayor's carnival parade
blurbs: {customer} organises the town carnival and needs a splendid classic car to lead the parade with the mayor waving from the back. Bunting provided.
It's {customer}. The carnival committee has voted, and our float this year is simply a lovely old car. Please do not ask. There was an incident with a float once.
{customer} needs a dignified car for the carnival parade. The town brass band will be walking behind, playing whatever they feel like.
success: {car} led the parade at a stately four miles an hour while the whole town waved, and {customer} declares it the finest carnival in living memory.
The mayor was so delighted with {car} that the wave lasted the entire route, and {customer} pays in full with a commemorative pennant.
{car} outshone every float in the parade, and {customer} says the marching brass band struck up a tune as it passed. Nobody knows which one.
mishap: The bunting snagged on {car}'s aerial and unwound gracefully down the high street, and {customer} calls it "an intentional design choice".
A marching tuba player collided gently with {car}'s wing mirror, and {customer} pays slightly less and offers the town's apologies.
The mayor's ceremonial chain jammed in {car}'s door, and the parade set off twelve minutes late to mild applause.
disaster: A runaway carnival float shaped like a teapot veered into the parade route, and {car} spent the afternoon in the duck pond while {customer} negotiated with a very wet mayor.
The carnival queen's confetti cannon went off inside {car}, and a passing swarm of bees decided the sticky paintwork was a picnic, while {customer} telephoned for backup.

name: Hen weekend
blurbs: {customer} is organising a hen weekend and wants a proper old car for a tour of the seaside towns. There will be glitter. There is always glitter.
It's {customer}. Ten of us, one classic car, a playlist of wedding discos, and a route involving four tea rooms. Bold, but fair.
{customer} needs something glamorous for a hen weekend. The bride-to-be has planned the whole thing on a napkin and refuses to change a detail.
success: Ten hens, one car, zero casualties, and {customer} reports the bride-to-be cried happily at the sight of {car} wearing the bow.
{car} survived the entire hen weekend with only glitter in the carpets, and {customer} says the tea room photos are already legendary.
The tour went off without a hitch and {car} was serenaded outside the third pub. {customer} pays in full and leaves a lanyard as a souvenir.
mishap: A sash of glitter glue dried overnight inside {car}, and {customer} promises the sparkle is "mostly decorative".
The hen party sang the entire playlist on the coast road, and {car}'s aerial vibrated in protest until someone sat on it. {customer} pays a little less.
One hen attempted a party trick on the bonnet of {car} and slid off with dignity mostly intact, and {customer} asks if the wax will fix it.
disaster: The hen party opened a farm gate to photograph some calves, and the calves found the leather seats of {car} delicious, while {customer} negotiated with a farmer.
The route planning by {customer} relied entirely on a fold-out map from a petrol station, and {car} ended up in a river ford that the map described as a shortcut.

name: Marriage proposal
blurbs: {customer} wants to propose to their partner in the back of a proper classic car. The ring is currently in a box the size of a shoebox.
It's {customer} here. My partner thinks we are going to the garden centre. I need something romantic with a gentle rumble.
{customer} needs a beautiful old car for a marriage proposal at sunset. The booking is for seven and the sunset, we are assured, is at six.
success: The proposal went perfectly with {car} as the backdrop, and {customer} reports the answer was yes before the question had finished.
{customer} slipped the ring onto the right finger beside {car}, and the engine idling to a stop got a round of applause from a passing bus.
The partner said yes at once, then spent ten minutes admiring {car} instead. {customer} calls it the cheapest victory of the year.
mishap: The ring fell through a gap in {car}'s seat and it took twenty minutes and a coat hanger to recover it. {customer} missed the sunset.
{customer} rehearsed the speech for weeks but got down on one knee in a puddle, and the proposal was finished from a picnic blanket.
A farmer's tractor chose the exact moment to trundle past the viewpoint, and {customer} had to pause the proposal until the ploughing was done.
disaster: The celebratory champagne cork fired off with some violence and landed in the engine bay of {car}, and {customer} spent the sunset fixing a hose instead of proposing.
A bold flock of geese surrounded {car} at the crucial moment and made off with the ring box, and {customer} chased them round the park for an hour.

name: Vicar's blessing tour
blurbs: {customer} is arranging a vicar's blessing tour of three parishes and needs something dignified for the drive between the churches.
It's {customer}. Our vicar wants to bless the harvest from the back of a classic car this year. Two hymns, one bonnet, no rushing.
{customer} needs a gentle old car to ferry the choir to a blessing by the harbour. The organ music will be provided on cassette.
success: The tour went beautifully and the vicar blessed {car} as well, free of charge. {customer} reports a fine turnout at all three parishes.
{car} purred between the churches like a low hymn, and {customer} says the parishioners queued afterwards to polish the headlamps.
The village turned out in force, the choir found its harmony by the second verse, and {customer} says {car} has never looked so holy.
mishap: A cassock caught in {car}'s door and the first blessing ran twenty minutes late. {customer} apologised to the whole parish with a fruitcake.
{customer} took a wrong turning and blessed the wrong village entirely, and the second parish had to wait for {car} to circle back.
A wasp got in during the second blessing and the congregation did an unplanned circuit of {car}. Nobody was hurt, but the hymn sheets scattered.
disaster: The travelling font tipped over on a country bend and soaked the back seat of {car}, and {customer} now owes the parish two towels and an apology.
A flock of sheep mistook {car} for the shepherd's truck and followed it into the churchyard, and {customer} is still writing letters to the parish council.

name: Amateur panto
blurbs: {customer} is directing the village panto and needs a classic car for the transformation scene. There will be glitter. There is always glitter.
It's {customer} from the village hall. Cinderella needs to arrive in something proper, and the pumpkin trailer broke down in March.
{customer} wants a beautiful old car for the panto finale. The stage is nine feet wide and the doors must open for the big number.
success: The finale brought the house down and {car} got the biggest cheer of the night. {customer} has already asked about next year.
{car} cleared the village hall doors with an inch to spare, and {customer} says the children booed the baddie for a full ten minutes.
The glitter settled, the audience roared, and {customer} admits {car} upstaged the dame in the largest wig of the century.
mishap: The stage crew covered {car} in glitter for the transformation scene, and three months later it still turns up in the upholstery. {customer} apologises.
A foam pumpkin fell off the flats and bounced off the roof of {car} mid-song. {customer} swears the audience thought it was part of the show.
{customer}'s dame got a sleeve caught in {car}'s window and improvised a whole new verse about it. The band kept playing. Just about.
disaster: The smoke machine jammed, the pantomime horse bolted, and {car} rolled through the scenery. {customer} is arguing with the insurance over an act of dame.
The village hall roof leaked during the matinee and a trough of water landed in {car}, and {customer} had to explain the ducks now living under the bonnet.

name: Celebrity chef taxi
blurbs: {customer} is producing a television cookery programme and needs a classic car to deliver a famous chef to a village fete. The chef is never on time.
It's {customer}. Our chef insists on arriving at food festivals in something handsome, and the last car still smells of previous ingredients.
{customer} needs a beautiful car for a chef touring four farm shops before lunch. The itinerary is ambitious and the pastry will not wait.
success: The chef arrived rested and almost on time, and {customer} says the fete scones sold out by noon. {car} gets a mention in the credits.
{car} swept into the festival to a small round of applause, and {customer} reports the chef wrote a dedication in pastry on the bonnet.
All four farm shops were visited, and {car} carried home more cheese than the boot could legally hold. {customer} pays in full, plus a wheel of stilton.
mishap: The chef insisted on a live demonstration in the passenger seat, and the smell of fried onions will never leave {car}. {customer} pays a little less.
A crate of prize tomatoes took a corner too briskly and redecorated the inside of {car}. {customer} apologised on television, twice.
{customer} took a detour after a van selling pastries, and the chef arrived late but called it 'research'. {car} smells of garlic.
disaster: The chef's portable fondue rig detonated over the back seat of {car}, and {customer} says the cheese is now a structural feature of the interior.
A herd of cows surrounded {car} outside the farm shop and licked the doors clean of the sauce spill, and {customer} filmed everything from a safe distance.
